positioning_analysis.reasoning: The 244-paper literature dataset confirms that while individual algorithms exist for component functions (e.g., Ethereum-based return anti-fraud in ESPRES [TRINETRA_0001], eBay dispute prediction models [TRINETRA_0197], and weight/scan anomaly detection), no single existing paper proposes a unified, end-to-end multi-stakeholder evidence reconciliation engine across seller, marketplace, logistics, and return center silos. Positioning 1 (Novel Research) is vulnerable because foundational algorithms for dispute prediction and blockchain provenance exist in top venues. Positioning 3 (Business System alone) understates the complex system integration novelties required for multi-stakeholder trust scoring and explainable evidence reconciliation.
required_literature_support: Component papers on return fraud detection and reverse logistics
Explainable AI (XAI) models for algorithmic decision transparency
positioning_analysis.current_literature_strength: High coverage of component problems (150 relevant papers, 40 core papers across OpenAlex, Crossref, and Semantic Scholar), but near-zero coverage of cross-organizational data reconciliation frameworks in commercial e-commerce settings.
positioning_analysis.critical_gap_for_chosen_positioning: Existing literature operates predominantly within single-organization data silos (e.g., warehouse logs alone or seller database alone) without reconciling conflicting evidence generated independently by opposing external stakeholders.
